scenario: A parent checks whether the bot is alive.
input: still working?
must: Reply naturally and briefly.
must_not: No lesson, image, or worksheet.

scenario: A parent pastes a teacher update as background context.
input: Sharing today's teacher note so you know what the class is working on.
must: Acknowledge and save context without manufacturing a lesson.
must_not: No visual or activity unless asked.

scenario: A parent gives product feedback about a prior answer.
input: That was much warmer, but the picture was not useful.
must: Treat this as output feedback.
must_not: Do not create another child activity now.

scenario: A parent asks an operational setup question.
input: How do I add another child?
must: Give a direct setup response.
must_not: No child-facing visual.

scenario: A first grader wonders about a friend's feelings.
input: Why was my friend mad at me?
must: Use careful possibilities and parent support.
must_not: No speculative illustration or worksheet.

scenario: A first grader asks about record-size robots.
input: What are the biggest robots in the world?
must: Clarify kinds of big and use an accurate qualitative comparison.
must_not: Generated art must not imply scale.

scenario: A first grader wants to see what an owl really looks like.
input: Can I see an owl's eyes and feathers up close?
must: Use a real, vetted wildlife photo.
must_not: Do not substitute cartoon art.

scenario: A first grader asks what Mars looks like.
input: What does the ground on Mars really look like?
must: Prefer a NASA surface photo with provenance.
must_not: Do not invent a fantasy landscape as evidence.

scenario: A child asks about a mechanism that is hard to photograph directly.
input: Why does ice float in water?
must: Use an accurate code-owned explanatory comparison if a visual is used.
must_not: A decorative image cannot teach density.

scenario: A child asks for imaginative pretend play.
input: Tell me a tiny adventure about a dragon who is scared of bubbles.
must: A playful illustration may spark the story.
must_not: No worksheet.

scenario: A child asks for a pretend dinosaur mission, not facts.
input: Can we go on a pretend dinosaur rescue mission?
must: Use story art only as imagination support.
must_not: Do not present generated dinosaurs as scientific reconstruction.

scenario: A parent wants something the child can actually use to compare paper airplanes.
input: Make a page to test two paper airplane designs and change one thing.
must: Supply sketch, test, change, and retest spaces.
must_not: Decorative airplane art is not the activity.

scenario: A first grader will place and reach paper leaves during sauropod pretend play.
input: Make the actual page we can use for a sauropod leaf reach game.
must: The printable must be part of the play.
must_not: Do not return only a pretty dinosaur.

scenario: A child will sort picture-word cards into two visible groups.
input: Make a cut-and-sort page for shells that are smooth or bumpy.
must: Include category areas and movable cards.
must_not: No generic prediction sheet.

scenario: A parent asks for a small matching game.
input: Make a tiny match-the-animal-to-its-home page.
must: Provide two complete shuffled sets.
must_not: Do not reveal every pair in the choices.

scenario: A child wants cards to order a seed's visible growth stages.
input: Can you make cards we put in order from seed to leaves?
must: Provide three to six movable steps.
must_not: Do not use generative art for exact sequence facts.

scenario: A first grader needs a large markable parts page.
input: Make a simple flower page where we can label root, stem, leaf, and flower.
must: Use a code-owned central diagram and callouts.
must_not: Do not rely on image-generated text.

scenario: A child will look outside and record cloud clues.
input: Give us a cloud detective page for looking out the window.
must: Provide a checklist and room to record visible clues.
must_not: No competition or quiz.

scenario: A child will predict and test two paper bridge shapes.
input: Make a page to predict which paper bridge holds more blocks, then test it.
must: Include prediction and result spaces.
must_not: Do not add exact invented results.

scenario: A child will measure one shadow several times.
input: Make a simple tally-and-graph page for our shadow measurements.
must: Include repeated rows and a simple graph.
must_not: Do not make the parent draw the graph.

scenario: A child wants an engineering challenge using paper.
input: Make a paper tower challenge page where we test and improve it.
must: Include sketch, test, one change, and retest.
must_not: No 3D printer or special kit.

scenario: A child likes mysteries and wants to reason from clues.
input: Make a mystery page about which animal left tracks near the bird seed.
must: Give clues, a best solution, and evidence space.
must_not: Do not turn it into a recall quiz.

scenario: A child wants to look for visible bird features.
input: Make a mini field guide page for noticing a robin's beak, wing, tail, and feet.
must: Use a vetted real robin photo and child-usable field marks.
must_not: A generic bird cartoon is insufficient.

scenario: A child will compare a stone and bark by sight and touch.
input: Make a page to compare smooth stone and rough bark and circle the clues.
must: Provide side-by-side evidence spaces.
must_not: No decorative-only nature scene.

scenario: A parent explicitly wants one sentence and no extras.
input: Just give me one sentence I can say. No picture, game, or worksheet.
must: Honor the exact boundary.
must_not: No visual or printable.
